title: 地球自转与昼夜
Earth’s spin and the day
question: 站在杭州，为什么每天都能看到日出？
Why does the Sun rise each day in Hangzhou?
summary: 跟随杭州穿过晨昏线，同时观察当地地平线上太阳的位置。
Follow Hangzhou across the day–night boundary and watch its local sky.
task: 把时间从清晨拖到正午。哪一刻太阳最高，竖杆的影子最短？
Scrub from dawn to noon. When is the Sun highest and a vertical pole’s shadow shortest?
answer: 当地太阳正午，太阳在这一天升得最高，竖杆的影子最短。这里用当地太阳时读数。
At local solar noon the Sun reaches its daily high point, giving a vertical pole its shortest shadow. The clock shows local solar time.

beats.zh: 想象你站在杭州的湖边。天边刚刚变亮，地球上的你正在向哪里转？
beats.en: Imagine standing beside a lake in Hangzhou. As the sky brightens, which way is the ground beneath you turning?

beats.zh: 看左边的金色标记，它就是杭州。此刻标记还在背对太阳的一侧。
beats.en: Find the gold marker on the globe. That is Hangzhou, still on the side that faces away from the Sun.

beats.zh: 地球从西向东自转。标记穿过明暗交界线时，右边的太阳从东方升起。
beats.en: Earth spins from west to east. As the marker crosses the boundary into daylight, the Sun rises on the eastern horizon.

beats.zh: 这条分隔昼夜的线叫晨昏线。太阳照亮约半个地球，城市随地球进入白天。
beats.en: The boundary between day and night is the terminator. Sunlight reaches about half of Earth at once, and our city turns into daylight.

beats.zh: 找到连接南北两极的地轴。赤道在两极正中间，纬度是零度。
beats.en: Trace the axis connecting the North and South Poles. Halfway between the poles is the equator, at zero degrees latitude.

beats.zh: 太阳在天上的东升西落，是地面观察者看到的视运动。试着想象把相机固定在地轴以外。
beats.en: The Sun's daily passage is an apparent motion seen from the ground. Imagine moving your camera off the spinning Earth and into space.

beats.zh: 太阳升得越来越高。到当地太阳正午，它在今天的天空中达到最高点。
beats.en: The Sun climbs higher. At local solar noon it reaches the highest point of its path across today's sky.

beats.zh: 接着把时间往前推。下午阳光渐斜，杭州再次来到晨昏线，太阳从西方落下。
beats.en: Move forward through the afternoon. Sunlight arrives at a shallower angle, and Hangzhou crosses the boundary again at sunset in the west.

beats.zh: 又一个正午大约要等二十四小时。这是一个平均太阳日，也是日常计时的依据。
beats.en: It takes about twenty-four hours on average to go from one solar noon to the next. This is a mean solar day.

beats.zh: 如果盯住的是远方恒星，地球转一圈约二十三小时五十六分。地球也在公转，所以要再多转一点，太阳才会回到正午。
beats.en: Measured against distant stars, a spin takes about twenty-three hours and fifty-six minutes. As Earth also advances in its orbit, it must turn a little farther for the Sun to return to noon.

beats.zh: 试着把标记停在日出的一刻。本章取春分附近的理想情况，时钟显示当地太阳时。
beats.en: Try stopping the marker at sunrise. This model uses ideal equinox geometry, and the clock reads local solar time.

title: 地球公转与四季
Earth’s orbit and the seasons
question: 六月同一天，为什么南北两地的白昼长短不同？
Why do the two hemispheres have different day lengths in June?
summary: 让倾斜的地球沿轨道运行，对比南北纬 30° 的太阳高度和白昼时长。
Carry a tilted Earth around the Sun and compare the daylight and noon Sun at 30° north and south.
task: 选六月至，再把地轴倾角切换成 0°。两地的白昼时长会怎样？
Choose the June solstice, then set the axial tilt to 0°. What happens to the two day lengths?
answer: 在这个圆轨道、零倾角模型中，两地全年都接近 12 小时白昼。恢复 23.4°，南北季节差异就回来了。
In this circular, zero-tilt model both sites receive about twelve hours of daylight year-round. Restore the tilt to bring back the seasonal contrast.

beats.zh: 地球除了自转，还绕太阳公转。走完一圈大约是一年，也就是三百六十五天多一点。
beats.en: Earth spins and also orbits the Sun. One trip takes a year, a little over three hundred and sixty-five days.

beats.zh: 盯住地球上的短轴线。地轴相对轨道面的垂线倾斜约二十三点四度。
beats.en: Follow the short line through Earth. Its axis tilts about twenty-three point four degrees away from the perpendicular to its orbital plane.

beats.zh: 地球沿轨道前进，地轴在这一年里大致指向同一片星空。六月，北极一端倾向太阳。
beats.en: As Earth moves, the axis points toward nearly the same distant stars. By the June solstice the northern end leans toward the Sun.

beats.zh: 比较右边两地。北纬三十度的正午太阳更高，又有更长的时间接收阳光。
beats.en: Compare the two observing sites. At thirty degrees north, the midday Sun stands higher and daylight lasts longer.

beats.zh: 太阳升得高，同样一束光覆盖的地面面积较小，单位面积接收的能量更多。把它和白昼长短联系起来想。
beats.en: With a higher Sun, a beam of light is spread over a smaller patch of ground. Each unit of area gets more energy. Combine that effect with longer daylight.

beats.zh: 南纬三十度则正好相反，太阳较低，白昼较短。同一时刻，两半球的季节相反。
beats.en: At thirty degrees south the midday Sun is lower and the days are shorter. The two hemispheres experience opposite seasons at the same time.

beats.zh: 走到九月分点，阳光直射赤道。忽略大气折射，两地的昼夜都接近等长。
beats.en: At the September equinox, sunlight falls directly on the equator. Ignoring atmospheric refraction, day and night are nearly equal at both sites.

beats.zh: 再走四分之一圈。到了十二月至，南极一端倾向太阳，南纬三十度的白昼变长。
beats.en: Travel another quarter orbit. At the December solstice the southern end leans toward the Sun, giving the southern site longer days.

beats.zh: 要检验离太阳远近的解释，看看同一天的两个半球。它们同在一个地球上，季节却正好相反。
beats.en: Test the idea that distance causes these seasons. Both hemispheres share essentially the same distance to the Sun on a given day, yet their seasons are opposite.

beats.zh: 现在临时把地轴扶正。保持相同的圆轨道，两地的白昼就一起回到十二小时。
beats.en: Now straighten the axis. With the same circular orbit, both sites return to twelve hours of daylight.

beats.zh: 恢复倾角再拖动一年。你可以分别追踪正午太阳高度和白昼时长，看它们一起变化。
beats.en: Restore the tilt and follow a year in the lab. Track both the noon Sun and the length of daylight as the seasons change.

title: 赤道与南北回归线
The equator and the tropics
question: 地球仪为什么要在南北纬 23.4° 各画一条线？
Why are there special lines at 23.4° north and south?
summary: 追踪太阳直射点的纬度，再从地面看一根竖杆的正午影子。
Track the latitude of the overhead Sun and watch a vertical pole’s noon shadow.
task: 把观测地点设为北回归线，再选六月至。此时竖杆的影长是多少？
Observe from the Tropic of Cancer at the June solstice. How long is the vertical pole’s shadow?
answer: 在理想模型中影长为零。太阳在正头顶，竖杆的影子落在杆脚。
Its length is zero in this ideal model. The Sun is directly overhead, so the pole casts its shadow at its base.

beats.zh: 在一块水平地面上竖起一根杆。如果太阳就在头顶，杆子的影子会落在哪里？
beats.en: Place a vertical pole on level ground. Where will its shadow fall if the Sun is directly overhead?

beats.zh: 地球上，正午太阳恰好在头顶的地方，叫太阳直射点。金点追踪的是它的纬度。
beats.en: The subsolar point is the place where the noon Sun shines straight down. The gold dot tracks its latitude.

beats.zh: 纬线与赤道平行。沿着同一条纬线向东或向西走，纬度始终一样，变化的是经度。
beats.en: Lines of latitude run parallel to the equator. Travel east or west along one and your latitude stays the same, even as your longitude changes.

beats.zh: 三月分点时，直射点在赤道。随着地球公转，这个纬度开始向北移动。
beats.en: At the March equinox the subsolar point lies on the equator. As Earth moves along its orbit, this latitude shifts north.

beats.zh: 六月至，它到达最北端，约北纬二十三点四度。这条纬线称为北回归线。
beats.en: At the June solstice it reaches its northern limit, about twenty-three point four degrees north. This is the Tropic of Cancer.

beats.zh: 看右边，观测地点就在北回归线。太阳直射的这一刻，竖杆的影子收到了杆脚。
beats.en: Our observer is now on the Tropic of Cancer. When the Sun is directly overhead, the pole’s shadow shrinks to its base.

beats.zh: 再沿着轨道前进，直射纬度折返向南。九月分点，它再次经过零度纬线。
beats.en: Continue around the orbit. The overhead Sun moves south and crosses the equator again at the September equinox.

beats.zh: 十二月至，它到达南回归线。换到南回归线观察，正午也能看见相同的零影长。
beats.en: In December it reaches the Tropic of Capricorn. An observer on that line now sees the same vanishing noon shadow.

beats.zh: 两条回归线的纬度，来自地轴倾角。它们标出了太阳可以直射的最北和最南边界。
beats.en: The latitudes of the tropics come from Earth’s tilt. They mark the northern and southern limits of the overhead Sun.

beats.zh: 赤道一年可经历两次太阳直射，回归线上大约一次。再向两极走，正午太阳就不会到达头顶。
beats.en: At the equator the Sun passes overhead twice a year, and on either tropic about once. Farther toward the poles, the noon Sun never reaches the zenith.

beats.zh: 在互动实验里，换三个不同的纬度，比较同一季节的正午太阳高度和杆影。
beats.en: In the lab, switch among the three marked latitudes. Compare the noon Sun and the pole’s shadow at the same time of year.

title: 月球公转与同步自转
The Moon’s synchronized spin
question: 月球明明在转，为什么地球上总看到大致相同的一面？
If the Moon spins, why do we see nearly the same face?
summary: 认准金色月面标记，在固定星空与地球两个参照系之间比较。
Track one gold surface marker from two perspectives: the fixed stars and Earth.
task: 在起点关闭月球自转，再拖到半圈。从地球还能看见标记吗？
Switch off the Moon’s spin at the start, then move half an orbit. Can Earth still see the marker?
answer: 此时标记转到背向地球的一侧。恢复同步自转，标记在绕行中一直朝向地球。
The marker now faces away from Earth. Restore synchronous rotation and the marker stays pointed toward Earth all around the orbit.

beats.zh: 挑一个月面地标来做实验。我们用金色圆环标出它，并把月面补亮，方便跟踪。
beats.en: Pick a landmark on the Moon. We mark it in gold and use even lighting so you can follow it throughout this experiment.

beats.zh: 左边从固定星空俯看月球绕地球，右边是在地球上看到的月面。先记住圆环的位置。
beats.en: On the left, watch the orbit against the fixed stars. On the right is the view from Earth. Notice where the circle starts.

beats.zh: 月球公转四分之一圈，同时绕自身转过九十度。标记的朝向随它一起改变。
beats.en: The Moon travels through a quarter orbit and turns ninety degrees on its own axis. Its marked face changes direction in space.

beats.zh: 再走到半圈，对照固定的星空，标记已经朝向相反的一边，却仍然对着地球。
beats.en: After half an orbit the marker points the opposite way relative to the stars, yet it still faces Earth.

beats.zh: 你也可以绕着一把椅子走，并始终面对椅背。走完一圈，你相对房间也恰好转了一圈。
beats.en: Try walking around a chair while always facing its back. After one circuit you have also turned all the way around relative to the room.

beats.zh: 相对于恒星，自转一周和公转一周都约二十七点三天。这种配合叫同步自转。
beats.en: Relative to the stars, both one spin and one orbit take about twenty-seven point three days. This is synchronous rotation.

beats.zh: 从起点重做实验。这一次临时关闭自转，让月球的朝向相对星空保持不变。
beats.en: Start the experiment again, this time with spin switched off. The marked face now keeps a fixed direction relative to distant stars.

beats.zh: 仍然绕着地球走。经过半圈时，地球上的观察者看到另一面，金色标记消失了。
beats.en: Keep the orbit moving. Halfway around, an observer on Earth sees the opposite face and the gold marker disappears.

beats.zh: 重新开启同步自转，金环又能持续朝向地球。比较这两次实验，就能分清自转和公转。
beats.en: Restore synchronous rotation and the landmark stays facing Earth. Compare these two runs to separate spin from orbital motion.

beats.zh: 朝向地球的一面称为近面，背向我们的一面称为远面。远面也有白天，阳光会照到它。
beats.en: The side facing Earth is the near side, and the other is the far side. The far side also has daylight when it faces the Sun.

beats.zh: 真实月球的视角还有轻微摇摆，叫天平动。这个模型先保留最主要的同步关系。
beats.en: The real Moon also appears to rock slightly, an effect called libration. Here we isolate its main, synchronized motion.

title: 月相与朔望月
Moon phases and the lunar month
question: 总是同一个月球，为什么一会儿像弯钩，一会儿又像圆盘？
Why does the same Moon change from a thin crescent to a full disk?
summary: 从太空看受光半球，从地球看其中可见的部分。
Compare the sunlit half in space with the part of that half visible from Earth.
task: 已知太阳照亮大约半个月球。上弦月时，从地球看，月面亮了多少？
Sunlight illuminates about half the lunar globe. At first quarter, how much of the disk seen from Earth is bright?
answer: 可见圆盘的一半发亮。“上弦”对应月相周期的四分之一；可见亮面比例是二分之一。
Half the visible disk is lit. First quarter marks one quarter of the phase cycle, while one half of the apparent disk is bright.

beats.zh: 回到真实的太阳照明。月球反射阳光，通常总有约半个球面被太阳照亮。
beats.en: Return to sunlight. The Moon shines by reflected light, and about half its globe normally faces the Sun.

beats.zh: 新月时，月球位于地球朝向太阳的一侧。受光面大多背对我们，圆盘几乎看不见。
beats.en: At new Moon, the Moon lies on the Sun-facing side of Earth. The lit half faces mostly away from us and the disk is hard to see.

beats.zh: 随着月球向前运行，我们开始看到一弯亮边。空间位置与地面所见对应起来了。
beats.en: As the Moon moves on, a thin bright crescent comes into view. Connect its position in space with what the observer sees.

beats.zh: 到了上弦月，月相周期走过四分之一。从地球看，月面圆盘正好有一半明亮。
beats.en: At first quarter, one quarter of the phase cycle has passed. From Earth, half of the apparent disk is now bright.

beats.zh: 想一想，另外半个圆盘为什么暗？从左图看，地球并没有挡住它的阳光，我们只是看见了部分月夜。
beats.en: Why is the rest of the disk dark? Earth is not blocking its sunlight in this view. Part of the visible lunar surface is simply experiencing night.

beats.zh: 继续到满月，月球位于地球背向太阳的一侧，我们几乎能看到整个受光的半球。
beats.en: Continue to full Moon. The Moon is on the side of Earth away from the Sun, so we can see almost the whole illuminated hemisphere.

beats.zh: 此时如果从月球近面回望地球，地球的受光面几乎背向月球。两个观察地点的亮面恰好互补。
beats.en: Now imagine looking back at Earth from the lunar near side. The sunlit half of Earth faces mostly away from the Moon. The two phases complement each other.

beats.zh: 接下来，明亮的部分开始缩小。到下弦月，又剩半个圆盘，但亮边已换到另一侧。
beats.en: The bright portion now decreases. At third quarter half the disk is lit again, with the bright side opposite to first quarter.

beats.zh: 这里统一把月面北方画在上面。真实夜空中的月牙会转过一个角度，取决于观察地点和时间。
beats.en: Here lunar north is up. The crescent can appear rotated in your own sky, depending on your location and the time of observation.

beats.zh: 从新月到下一次新月，平均约二十九点五天，称为一个朔望月。
beats.en: From one new Moon to the next takes about twenty-nine and a half days on average. This is the synodic month.

beats.zh: 它比恒星月稍长，因为地球也在绕太阳前进。月球要再多走一段，才恢复相同的日地月夹角。
beats.en: This takes longer than an orbit relative to the stars. Earth also moves around the Sun, so the Moon must travel farther to recover the same Sun–Earth–Moon geometry.

title: 日食、月食与轨道交点
Eclipses and orbital nodes
question: 新月和满月每月都有，为什么日食和月食不每月都发生？
Why don’t eclipses happen at every new or full Moon?
summary: 比较两种阴影的去向，再把新月或满月移近和移离轨道交点。
Trace two different shadows, then compare an alignment near a node with one far from it.
task: 选择满月、交点附近，把时间拖到最接近时。谁进入了谁的影子？
Choose full Moon near a node and move to closest alignment. Which body enters which shadow?
answer: 地球挡住射向月球的阳光，月球进入地球本影，地球夜半球上能看到月食。
Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon. The Moon enters Earth’s umbra, and observers on Earth’s night side can see a lunar eclipse.

beats.zh: 先看新月附近。太阳、月球和地球若排得足够直，月球就会遮住地面观察者眼中的太阳。
beats.en: Start near new Moon. When Sun, Moon and Earth line up closely enough, the Moon can cover the Sun in an observer’s sky.

beats.zh: 月影落在地球上。处于半影的观察者看到日偏食，本影扫过的狭窄区域可见日全食。
beats.en: The Moon casts a shadow on Earth. Observers in the penumbra see a partial eclipse, while people in the narrow umbra can see a total solar eclipse.

beats.zh: 右边模拟位于全食带的观察者。食甚时明亮的日面被盖住，外围日冕显现出来。
beats.en: The right view places us in the path of totality. At maximum eclipse the bright solar disk is covered and the outer corona becomes visible.

beats.zh: 换到满月附近，这次地球在中间。太阳光被地球挡住，月球走进地球的影子。
beats.en: Switch to full Moon. Now Earth is in the middle. It blocks sunlight and the Moon moves into Earth’s shadow.

beats.zh: 日食时，是否看见全食取决于你站在哪里。月食时，只要月球在当地地平线上方，天气合适，就有机会看到。
beats.en: For a solar eclipse, your location determines whether you see totality. A lunar eclipse is visible much more widely, wherever the Moon is above the horizon and skies are clear.

beats.zh: 当月面全部进入本影，就发生月全食。穿过地球大气后折射过去的红光，能让月面呈现暗红色。
beats.en: When the whole Moon enters the umbra, the lunar eclipse is total. Red light bent through Earth’s atmosphere can give the Moon a dim copper color.

beats.zh: 为什么这种对齐这么难？月球轨道面相对地球公转轨道面倾斜约五点一度。
beats.en: Why is this alignment uncommon? The Moon's orbital plane is tilted by about five point one degrees relative to the plane of Earth's orbit.

beats.zh: 两平面相交，月球穿过地球轨道面的位置叫交点。把新月移离交点，月影会掠过地球旁边。
beats.en: The Moon crosses Earth's orbital plane at two nodes. Move the new Moon away from a node and its shadow sweeps past Earth.

beats.zh: 满月也一样。离交点较远时，月球从地球本影上方或下方经过，仍然是一轮明亮的满月。
beats.en: The same test works at full Moon. Far from a node, the Moon passes above or below the umbra and stays bright.

beats.zh: 把俯视想象成把两条轨道压在一张纸上，它会隐藏高低的差别。所以判断有无食，还要从侧面检查。
beats.en: Imagine flattening both orbits onto a sheet of paper. A top view hides their difference in height, so use a side view to check whether the shadows really meet.

beats.zh: 在实验台对比四种组合。先辨认谁在中间，再检查是否靠近交点，就能判断阴影落在哪里。
beats.en: Try all four combinations in the lab. Identify the body in the middle, then check the node alignment to predict where the shadow falls.
